flawed_step: The proof would need Hall's condition |N(S)| >= |S| for every S ⊆ A. Degree counting only gives |S| <= 2|N(S)|, hence |N(S)| >= |S|/2; the step from the degree assumptions to Hall's condition is unjustified.
counterexample: Let A={a1,a2}, B={b}, and E={{a1,b},{a2,b}}. Each vertex of A has degree 1, and b has degree 2, so all hypotheses hold. Any matching contains at most one edge because both edges share b. Thus no matching saturates both a1 and a2.
assessment_summary: The statement is false: two vertices in A may share a single common neighbor in B. The bound degree(b) <= 2 permits this obstruction.
